method.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: a 1024x1024 base-color UV texture atlas for the existing animated Khronos red fox 3D mesh.
Input image 1 is the exact edit target, NOT a drawing reference. Keep the square canvas, all UV islands, every island silhouette, positions, gaps, orientation, proportions, black nose pixels, eye pixels, and the existing orange/cream/dark-brown marking boundaries registered exactly to this original image. Do not draw a fox, a scene, labels, a UV wireframe, padding, or a border.
Change only the flat surface appearance inside the existing colored islands to believable red fox fur: subtle densely packed fine rust and ochre guard hairs over soft underfur in orange regions; warm ivory short fur in cream regions; dark charcoal-brown dense fur on paws and ears. Keep the same overall color masses and rough matte material. Add low-contrast natural directional fiber variation at a fine scale, not large spots or stripes. The two large body-side islands flow from nose at their outside edge toward hindquarters; leg fur follows the long direction of each small upper island. Preserve dark olive unused background exactly. This is an unlit albedo map: no cast shadows, specular lighting, ambient occlusion, baked highlights or 3D perspective. Technical UV correspondence matters more than decorative detail. Output a single opaque square texture.

attribution: Model/atlas: PixelMannen; rigging and animation: tomkranis; glTF conversion: @AsoboStudio and @scurest; generated fur surface edit: AxiomsAwake contributors using built-in image_gen (2026).
notes: Original GLB, embedded texture and refined GLB bytes remain unchanged; the native setting composes this external albedo override on independent per-actor materials.
Generated output is 1254 square rather than requested 1024; normalized UV coordinates are unchanged.
Coarse 4px normalized sampling places 29713 of 30160 original orange/cream samples in the same broad marking category; this approximate classifier is not proof of seamless texture correspondence.
Image generation adds surface detail; it does not prove anatomical or motion quality.
